module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 898

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/898](https://www.erdosproblems.com/898)
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved*.
  (1982), 59--79.
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erd%C5%91s%E2%80%93Mordell_inequality)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Affine EuclideanGeometry

namespace Erdos898

/--
If $A,B,C\in \mathbb{R}^2$ form a triangle and $P$ is a point in the interior then, if $N$ is
where the perpendicular from $P$ to $AB$ meets the triangle, and similarly for $M$ and $L$,
$$
\overline{PA}+\overline{PB}+\overline{PC}\geq 2(\overline{PM}+\overline{PN}+\overline{PL}).
$$

Conjectured by Erdős in 1932 (according to [Er82e]) and proved by Mordell soon afterwards, now
known as the Erdős-Mordell inequality.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 51, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos898.lean"]
theorem erdos_898 (A B C P L M N : ℝ²) (hABC : AffineIndependent ℝ ![A, B, C])
    (hP : P ∈ interior (convexHull ℝ ({A, B, C} : Set ℝ²)))
    (hN : N ∈ line[ℝ, A, B]) (hPN : line[ℝ, P, N].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, A, B].direction)
    (hM : M ∈ line[ℝ, B, C]) (hPM : line[ℝ, P, M].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, B, C].direction)
    (hL : L ∈ line[ℝ, C, A]) (hPL : line[ℝ, P, L].direction ⟂ line[ℝ, C, A].direction) :
    dist P A + dist P B + dist P C ≥ 2 * (dist P M + dist P N + dist P L) := by
  sorry

end Erdos898

reformulations.difference: The perpendicular feet are universally quantified points constrained by side-line membership and orthogonality of line directions, rather than defined as orthogonal projections.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each side, the two hypotheses hold exactly when the designated foot equals the orthogonal projection of P onto that side's supporting line. Such a point exists uniquely. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, I proved this characterization and the equivalence between the universally quantified feet formulation and the projection-distance inequality, without using the theorem under review. Wikipedia explicitly allows feet outside the side segments in obtuse triangles.

sources_consulted: Erdős, Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved (1982), p. 61, geometry §1: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1982-33.pdf
review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the cited Erdős–Mordell inequality. Lean checks confirmed the Euclidean metric, noncollinearity characterization, satisfiable triangle/interior hypotheses, and degenerate-case behavior. The primary paper supports both the solved status and the docstring's 1932 date. The linked external proof checks with only standard axioms after one definitional-unfolding adjustment for Lean 4.33.1; its stated target is 4.29.1. erdosproblems.com/898 remained Cloudflare-blocked, but the cited primary paper and Wikipedia were available and sufficient to verify the statement.
